title: Decision Trees & Random Forests
summary: Grow a decision tree greedily by picking the split that most reduces Gini impurity or entropy, stop it before it memorizes noise, then average away its variance by bagging many trees into a random forest.
takeaways: Gini (1 − Σp²) and entropy (−Σp·log2 p) both measure how mixed a node is, and both are 0 when it's pure.
A split's information gain is the parent's impurity minus the size-weighted impurity of its children.
Trees are grown greedily, one split at a time. max_depth and min_samples_split stop them from memorizing noise.
Bagging trains each tree on a bootstrap sample and takes a majority vote. Random forests also randomize features, which makes the trees less correlated.

flow.title: Growing a tree, then a forest

steps.label: Measure impurity
steps.detail: Compute Gini or entropy of the labels at the node.

steps.label: Search splits
steps.detail: For every feature and midpoint threshold, send x ≤ t left and the rest right.

steps.label: Pick the best gain
steps.detail: gain = H(parent) − (n_L/n)·H(L) − (n_R/n)·H(R). Keep the largest positive one.

steps.label: Recurse or stop
steps.detail: Split and recurse, or make a majority-class leaf at max_depth, below min_samples_split, or with no gain.

steps.label: Bag and vote
steps.detail: Fit many trees on bootstrap samples from one seeded rng, then predict by majority vote.

terms.definition: 1 − Σ p_k²: the chance that two labels drawn at random from the node disagree.
−Σ p_k·log2 p_k: the average number of bits needed to encode a label from the node.
The drop in impurity from parent to children, with each child weighted by its fraction of the rows.
n rows drawn with replacement from n. On average it contains about 63.2% of the distinct rows.
Bootstrap aggregating: train one model per bootstrap sample and combine them by voting or averaging.
The roughly 36.8% of rows a tree never saw. They give a free validation estimate.
